summary.title: MQTT broker from scratch #4 - Data structures
summary.one_liner: You learn how to implement a generic hashtable (with CRC32 hashing, linear probing and rehashing) and a singly-linked list with O(1) head and tail insertion in C, as building blocks for an MQTT broker.
keywords: linked list head and tail pointers
takeaways: A hashtable maps string keys to indexes via a hash function, using linear probing to resolve collisions and doubling its size when half full.
The hash function here is CRC32 of the key, mixed with Robert Jenkins' mix function and Knuth's multiplicative method, with the author noting Murmur3 as another option.
A singly-linked list with head and tail pointers gives O(1) insertion at both ends, which the author judged sufficient over a vector.
Structures store void pointers with optional destructors so that the containers stay generic.
Part 5 of the series covers a tree to manage hierarchical topics; a trie is mentioned as key for topic management.
summary.summary: The author continues a series on writing an MQTT broker in C by implementing common data structures needed by the server. The post presents a generic hashtable (buckets array, CRC32 hash, Knuth multiplicative method, linear probing with a maximum chain length, and rehashing to double size) with full C source for the header and implementation. It then shows a generic singly-linked list with head and tail pointers for O(1) insertion at either end, including push, remove, sort-insert and bisect helpers. A trie is mentioned as planned for topic management, to be covered in Part 5.
